summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted with an acute flare characterized by epigastric pain, nausea, and poor oral intake. She also reported new right lower quadrant pain, likely due to adhesions, though imaging showed no obstruction. She was managed with IV fluids, pain control, and antiemetics. A PICC line was placed on hospital day 3, and TPN was initiated on day 4 to support nutrition. Her lipase normalized, pain improved, and she advanced to a regular diet. Pancytopenia was noted but stable, presumed related to malnutrition, with plans for outpatient follow-up. Constipation was treated with increased bowel regimen. She remained on home medications for depression, overactive bladder, and GERD. She was discharged home with a 3-week TPN plan, visiting nurse services, and follow-up arranged with her GI and primary care providers.
